breakdown.description: The prompt forms the torsional strain energy with the bending second moment I instead of the polar moment J, which is inconsistent with torsion theory.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses the polar moment J = π d^4/32 in the torsional strain-energy expression. While it mentions computing I = π d^4/64 'for reference,' it explicitly states to use J (not I) in the strain energy formula, and all subsequent calculations use J. This aligns with the ground truth, which omits the erroneous instruction to use I in place of J entirely. The core inconsistency — using the bending second moment I instead of the polar moment J in the torsional strain energy — has been resolved.
